name: leather_wrap
summary: The grip: a leather cord wound round the tang, in bands, worn where a hand has held it.
why: Metallic 0.0, and this is the one that matters most in the picture. Everything about a
dielectric is different from a metal: it keeps its own colour, its highlight is white
rather than tinted, and it has a diffuse term at all. A grip left metallic is a grip
made of dark chrome, which is what MU's flat art turns into the moment a light hits it.
Rough, at 0.72. Leather scatters; there is no sharp highlight anywhere on it, and a
wound grip is rougher still because the bands break up whatever is left.
The grain is the winding. It runs across the grip rather than along it, at a scale that
puts a band every few millimetres, which is what a cord wrap is.
Grip only. Anything flat wants leather instead, and this is worth saying here rather than
leaving it to be rediscovered: the grain is bands along one axis, which is the subject on a
cord wound round a tang and corduroy on anything broader. It has now caught a quiver's bag
and a mace's grip panel in one batch, and leather.json's own record of a weave measured at
